nodes.name: Input
nodes.notes: Frozen contract (design S-F). Renaming a field here migrates ALL callers in the same change. typeVersion 1.1 and not 1.2: the MCP catalog offers 1.2 but this instance does not have it installed and the node showed up as 'Install this node to use it'. 1.1 already supports inputSource workflowInputs.

nodes.name: Build Message
nodes.notes: S-E: validates and builds BEFORE claiming. Blowing up here writes no key; blowing up later burns the patient.

nodes.name: Claim Key
nodes.notes: INV-3: atomic claim. NO onError on purpose: if the INSERT fails the workflow has to crash (INV-2).

parameters.query:
insert into bot.sends
  (unique_key, patient_id, last_name, phone, milestone, template, status)
values ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, 'pending')
on conflict (unique_key) do nothing
returning unique_key;

nodes.name: Claimed?
nodes.notes: typeValidation loose on purpose: with alwaysOutputData the 'already existed' case arrives as {} and unique_key is undefined. In strict mode that throws an error instead of taking the false branch.

nodes.name: Notify Existing Key
nodes.notes: INV-15: no parse_mode. Keys carry underscores and an unbalanced Markdown kills the alert with a 400. | INV-15 (corrected 2026-09-08): parse_mode has NO 'None' option and omitting it does NOT disable parsing - n8n sends Markdown anyway, and a key with an odd number of underscores kills the alert with a 400. HTML is set explicitly and & < > are escaped in every interpolation.

parameters.text:
=KEY ALREADY EXISTED - nothing was sent

Key: {{ String($('Input').item.json.unique_key).replaceAll('&','&').replaceAll('<','<').replaceAll('>','>') }}
Patient: {{ String($('Input').item.json.last_name).replaceAll('&','&').replaceAll('<','<').replaceAll('>','>') }} (milestone {{ String($('Input').item.json.milestone).replaceAll('&','&').replaceAll('<','<').replaceAll('>','>') }})

The orchestrator's existing-keys filter let through a candidate who was already contacted. Check that filter. Nothing was sent.

assignments.name: reason
assignments.value: the key already existed; nothing was sent

nodes.name: Send
nodes.notes: INV-4: retryOnFail FALSE - the endpoint accepts no idempotency key, so retrying means duplicating. neverError off: with it ON, 4xx responses would leave through the success branch and be marked 'sent' for a message that never went out. YCloud API credential plugged in on 2026-09-06: from then on this node CAN send real WhatsApp messages.

nodes.name: Classify Failure
nodes.notes: INV-5. A 502 goes to ambiguous, not to failed: nobody claimed the message did not go out.

nodes.name: Record Result
nodes.notes: S-G: the AND status='pending' prevents overwriting a 'delivered' that the webhook already wrote. INV-9: 'delivered' is never written here. queryReplacement goes as an ARRAY, not as a comma-separated list: with commas, an empty value is dropped and shifts the positions, and a comma inside error_message would split the value in two. | 2026-09-08: ycloud_id as $6 (at the end, so the existing positions do not shift). The delivery webhook also writes it, with coalesce.

parameters.query:
update bot.sends
   set status        = $2,
       wamid         = coalesce(nullif($3, ''), wamid),
       ycloud_id     = coalesce(nullif($6, ''), ycloud_id),
       error_code    = nullif($4, ''),
       error_message = nullif($5, ''),
       sent_at       = case when $2 = 'sent' then now() else sent_at end,
       closed_at     = case when $2 = 'failed' then now() else closed_at end
 where unique_key = $1
   and status = 'pending'
returning status, error_code, error_message;

nodes.name: Needs Alert?
nodes.notes: A single condition covers failed, ambiguous and the zero-rows case (where status comes back empty and is not 'sent' either).

nodes.name: Notify
nodes.notes: INV-15: no parse_mode. retryOnFail YES: retrying an alert cannot duplicate a message to a patient. | INV-15 (corrected 2026-09-08): parse_mode has NO 'None' option and omitting it does NOT disable parsing - n8n sends Markdown anyway, and a key with an odd number of underscores kills the alert with a 400. HTML is set explicitly and & < > are escaped in every interpolation.
